statement: Stamps are worth 1, 2 and 5 cents. In how many different ways can you make exactly 10 cents? (The order of the stamps does not matter.)

choices.misconception: I left out the 1-cent stamps and only used 2-cent and 5-cent ones.
I only counted the ways that use at least one 5-cent stamp.
I forgot the way that uses two 5-cent stamps.

hints: Sort the ways by how many 5-cent stamps they use.
Do casework on the biggest stamp: no 5-cent stamps, one, or two. In each case the rest is made from 1s and 2s, so count how many 2-cent stamps can be used.
With no 5s, use 0 to 5 two-cent stamps. With one 5, use 0 to 2 two-cent stamps. With two 5s, nothing else.

solutions.reliable: Case 0 fives: the 10 cents is made of 2s and 1s, with 0, 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5 twos, so 6 ways. Case 1 five: 5 cents of 2s and 1s, with 0, 1 or 2 twos, so 3 ways. Case 2 fives: 1 way. Total 6 + 3 + 1 = 10. The transferable idea: in a making-amounts count, fix the biggest piece first and count the rest case by case.

whyOnTest: Counting ways to make an amount needs casework organised by the largest coin, or ways get missed.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
